# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker. =====README=====
# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

A Docker boundary can make accidental edits outside the application files impossible when the container is given only the application directory. ## Recommended design Keep the detached sparse Git worktree as the host-side source boundary, then run OpenCode inside a non-root Docker container: 1. Create `/tmp/opencode-worktree-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}` from the selected base branch, containing only the application files. 2. Mount the application directory at `/workspace/app` in the container. 3. OpenCode writes files but does not commit or push; the host sync helper copies only the application files, validates the path scope, commits, and pushes with `--force-with-lease`. ## Git boundary options Mounting only the application files gives the strongest scope protection, but OpenCode cannot inspect Git history or commit directly. Mounting the complete sparse worktree would allow direct Git operations, but requires exposing Git metadata, handling container path references and UID permissions, and weakens the protection against out-of-scope changes. Host-side synchronization is preferred. ## Risks to validate before implementation - Docker availability and permissions on the temporary AgentsWeb worker. - Non-root container UID ownership of generated files. - Playwright/Chromium dependencies and browser sandbox behavior. - App, OpenCode Web, SSH, and Cloudflare tunnel networking and port mapping. - Bun/npm/pnpm caches without mounting host credentials or the Docker socket. - Cleanup of containers, volumes, and worktrees after cancellation or failure. ## Acceptance criteria - The container can read/write only the isolated application directory. - A standard `OpenCode`-labeled run completes browser and public URL verification. - The host sync step rejects any changed path outside the application files. - Worker-generated files survive container exit and are committed by the host. ==> /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md <== # Pass OpenCode OAuth credentials through the worker environment OpenCode supports `OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT` as an environment-only auth path. playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags

  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item

  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

## Objective
- Build a playable 3D Pokémon-style RPG set in Jamaica, with creatures based on mythology from different cultures and shooter mechanics included.

## Requirements
- 3D (Three.js) browser game.
- Jamaica-inspired setting.
- Monster roster drawn from different world mythologies.
- Include shooter mechanics.
- Responsive mobile/touch support expected by repository conventions.

## Decisions
- Title: **SOUL YARD — Legends of Pimento Isle**.
- Third-person over-the-shoulder action shooter, not turn-based combat.
- Shooter loop: weaken wild spirits with aether bolts, then throw soul orbs to capture/bond them.
- Jamaica-inspired fictional island zones: Pimento Beach, Nine Mile Village, Blue Mountain Rise, Luminous Reef, Silk Cotton Grove.
- Eight mythic creatures: Anansi, Rolling Calf, Mami Wata, Quetzalcoatl, Nian, Bakunawa, Kitsune, Raven.
- Three Warden bosses plus final boss Anansi Unbound; quest progression through shrine purification.
- Party of 4 active bonds, companion AI attacks, elemental type wheel, procedural models/audio/textures, no external 3D/audio assets.
- Desktop + mobile controls, HUD, minimap, compendium, dialogue, pause, death, victory screens.
- Vite + Three.js, generated portrait screenshots via offscreen renderer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Initialized project files: `package.json`, `index.html`, `src/style.css`.
- Downloaded local fonts: `public/fonts/fraunces.woff2`, `public/fonts/outfit.woff2`.
- Implemented utility/terrain/constants modules:

  - `src/constants.js`

- Implemented audio synth: `src/audio.js`.
- Implemented input handling: `src/input.js`.
- Implemented creature AI/combat/bosses: `src/creatures.js`.
- Implemented player mechanics/camera/companion: `src/player.js`.
- Implemented HUD/codex/dialogue/minimap: `src/hud.js`.
- Implemented main game orchestration: `src/main.js`.

### Active
- First complete integration pass just finished writing `src/main.js`; no build, tests, or browser verification has run yet.
- Known likely bugs still need fixing:
  - `src/player.js` calls `input.consumeSlot()` twice in one frame.

  - `src/creatures.js` uses `setTimeout` for melee damage and boss lunge; verify no stale callbacks after pause/death.
  - Boss `captureCreature()` calls `capture()` then may schedule model hide; ensure boss array/cleanup works.
  - `finalCheck(c)` only returns true for final boss; normal victory path logic must be reviewed.

### Blocked
- Not blocked, but no verification has been performed.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

186:           x = spawn.x + Math.cos(a) * r
187:           z = spawn.z + Math.sin(a) * r
188:           guard++
189:         } while (guard < 30 && (terrainHeight(x, z) < 1.4 || this.world.isBlocked(x, z, 1.4) || Math.hypot(x - 9, z - 84) < 8))
190:         if (terrainHeight(x, z) < 1.2) continue
191:         const level = Math.floor(range(Math.random, spawn.levels[0], spawn.levels[1] + 1))
192:         const c = new Creature(def, { game: this, scene: this.scene, x, z, level })

288:   // ------------------------------------------------------------------ LOOP
289:   loop() {
290:     requestAnimationFrame(() => this.loop())
291:     const raw = Math.min(0.05, this.clock.getDelta())
292:     this.time += raw
293:     this.fpsFrames++
294:     this.fpsAccum += raw
295:     if (this.fpsAccum > 0.75) { this.fps = Math.round(this.fpsFrames / this.fpsAccum); this.fpsFrames = 0; this.fpsAccum = 0 }
296:     if (this.slowmo > 0) {
297:       this.slowmo -= raw
298:       this.timeScale = lerp(this.timeScale, 0.28, 0.25)
299:     } else {
300:       this.timeScale = lerp(this.timeScale, 1, 0.12)
301:     }
302:     const dt = raw * (this.mode === 'playing' ? this.timeScale : 1)
303:     this.world?.update(raw, this.time)
304: 
305:     if (this.mode === 'title') this.updateTitle(raw)
306:     else if (this.mode === 'playing') this.updatePlaying(dt, raw)
307:     else if (this.mode === 'dialogue') this.updateDialogueInput()
308: 
309:     this.updateEffects(raw)
310:     this.renderFrame(raw)
311:   }

514:   setWardenQuest() {
515:     const remaining = BOSSES.filter(b => !b.final && !this.purified.has(b.shrine))
516:     const count = this.purified.size
517:     if (remaining.length === 0) {
518:       this.questStage = 3
519:       this.hud.setQuest({
520:         title: 'The Unbound Trickster',
521:         desc: 'The Great Silk Cotton is open. Face Anansi beneath its branches.',
522:         progress: 1,
523:         progressText: '3 / 3 wardens',
524:         target: { x: SILK_TREE.x, z: SILK_TREE.z },
525:       })
526:       this.hud.setObjectives([{ x: SILK_TREE.x, z: SILK_TREE.z, kind: 'boss', label: 'Anansi Unbound' }])
527:       this.world.showWaypoint('tree')
528:       this.unlockFinal()
529:       return
530:     }
531:     // Nearest shrine becomes the waypoint.
532:     let nearest = remaining[0], nd = Infinity

539:     this.hud.setQuest({
540:       title: 'The Three Wardens',
541:       desc: 'Purify the mountain, reef and canopy shrines.',
542:       progress: count / 3,
543:       progressText: `${count} / 3 wardens`,
544:       target: { x: SHRINES[nearest.shrine].x, z: SHRINES[nearest.shrine].z },

547:       x: SHRINES[b.shrine].x, z: SHRINES[b.shrine].z, kind: 'boss', label: b.name,
548:     })))

820:   // ------------------------------------------------------------------ EFFECT UPDATES
821:   updateProjectiles(dt) {
822:     const player = this.player
823:     for (let i = this.playerOrbs.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
824:       const o = this.playerOrbs[i]
825:       o.life -= dt
826:       o.velocity.y -= 15 * dt
827:       o.model.position.addScaledVector(o.velocity, dt)
828:       o.model.userData.spin?.(this.time)
829:       o.model.rotation.x += dt * 4
830:       o.trail -= dt
831:       if (o.trail <= 0) {
832:         o.trail = 0.05
833:         this.spawnDashTrail(o.model.position.clone(), 0x8ff0ce)
834:       }
835:       let remove = false
836:       let captured = false
837:       for (const c of this.creatures) {
838:         if (!c.alive && !c.weakened) continue
839:         const center = c.model.position.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, c.height * 0.45, 0))
840:         const d = o.model.position.distanceTo(center)
841:         if (d < c.hitRadius + 0.55) {
842:           if (c.captureReady) {
843:             this.captureCreature(c)
844:             captured = true
845:           } else {
846:             this.burst(o.model.position.clone(), 0x8ff0ce, 12, 4)
847:             this.hud.toast('soul shielded', 'Weaken the spirit until its soul is exposed.', 'coral')
848:             this.audio.sfx('hit')
849:           }
850:           remove = true
851:           break
852:         }
853:       }
854:       if (!captured && o.model.position.y < terrainHeight(o.model.position.x, o.model.position.z) + 0.2) {
855:         this.burst(o.model.position.clone(), 0x37d6a5, 10, 4)
856:         remove = true
857:       }
858:       if (o.life <= 0) {
859:         this.burst(o.model.position.clone(), 0x37d6a5, 8, 3)
860:         remove = true
861:       }
862:       if (remove) {
863:         this.scene.remove(o.model)
864:         o.model.traverse(m => { if (m.isMesh) { m.geometry?.dispose?.(); m.material?.dispose?.() } if (m.isSprite) m.material?.dispose?.() })
865:         this.playerOrbs.splice(i, 1)
866:       }
867:     }
868: 
869:     for (let i = this.enemyOrbs.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
870:       const o = this.enemyOrbs[i]
871:       o.life -= dt
872:       if (o.homing > 0) {
873:         const target = player.position.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.0, 0))
874:         const steer = target.sub(o.model.position).normalize().multiplyScalar(o.homing * dt * 12)
875:         o.velocity.add(steer)
876:       }
877:       if (o.gravity) o.velocity.y -= o.gravity * dt
878:       o.model.position.addScaledVector(o.velocity, dt)
879:       const chest = player.position.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.0, 0))
880:       if (o.model.position.distanceTo(chest) < 0.85 + o.radius) {
881:         player.takeDamage(o.damage, null)
882:         this.burst(o.model.position.clone(), o.color, 14, 4)
883:         this.scene.remove(o.model)
884:         this.enemyOrbs.splice(i, 1)
885:         continue
886:       }
887:       if (o.model.position.y < terrainHeight(o.model.position.x, o.model.position.z) + 0.15 || o.life <= 0) {
888:         this.burst(o.model.position.clone(), o.color, 8, 3)
889:         this.scene.remove(o.model)
890:         this.enemyOrbs.splice(i, 1)
891:       }
892:     }
893: 
894:     for (let i = this.allyBolts.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
895:       const b = this.allyBolts[i]
896:       b.life -= dt
897:       const t = b.target
898:       if (!t || !t.alive) {
899:         this.dashTrails.push({ mesh: b.model, life: 0.25, max: 0.25 })
900:         this.allyBolts.splice(i, 1)
901:         continue
902:       }
903:       const goal = t.model.position.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, t.height * 0.5, 0))
904:       const dir = goal.clone().sub(b.model.position)
905:       const dist = dir.length()
906:       if (dist < 1.2) {
907:         t.takeDamage(b.damage, b.type, { critChance: this.player.critChance })
908:         this.burst(goal, b.color, 10, 4)
909:         this.scene.remove(b.model)
910:         this.allyBolts.splice(i, 1)
911:         continue
912:       }
913:       b.model.position.addScaledVector(dir.normalize(), b.speed * dt)
914:       if (b.life <= 0) { this.scene.remove(b.model); this.allyBolts.splice(i, 1) }
915:     }
916:   }

918:   updateBossDashes(dt) {
919:     for (let i = this.bossDashes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
920:       const d = this.bossDashes[i]
921:       d.time -= dt
922:       const b = d.boss
923:       if (!b || !b.alive) { this.bossDashes.splice(i, 1); continue }
924:       const nx = b.model.position.x + d.dir.x * d.speed * dt
925:       const nz = b.model.position.z + d.dir.z * d.speed * dt
926:       if (!this.world.isBlocked(nx, nz, b.hitRadius * 0.4)) {
927:         b.model.position.x = nx
928:         b.model.position.z = nz
929:       }
930:       b.model.position.y = terrainHeight(b.model.position.x, b.model.position.z) + (b.fly ? b.scale * 2 : 0)
931:       if (!d.hit) {
932:         const dist = Math.hypot(b.model.position.x - this.player.position.x, b.model.position.z - this.player.position.z)
933:         if (dist < b.hitRadius + 1.1) {
934:           d.hit = true
935:           this.player.takeDamage(b.damage * 1.2, b)
936:           this.cameraKick(0.15)
937:         }
938:       }
939:       if (Math.random() < 0.5) this.spawnDashTrail(b.model.position.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.6, 0)), b.def.colors.glow)
940:       if (d.time <= 0) this.bossDashes.splice(i, 1)
941:     }
942:   }

944:   updateEffects(dt) {
945:     for (let i = this.bursts.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
946:       const b = this.bursts[i]
947:       b.life -= dt
948:       const arr = b.geo.attributes.position.array
949:       for (let j = 0; j < b.velocities.length; j++) {
950:         const v = b.velocities[j]
951:         arr[j * 3] += v.x * dt
952:         arr[j * 3 + 1] += v.y * dt
953:         arr[j * 3 + 2] += v.z * dt
954:         v.y -= b.gravity * dt
955:       }
956:       b.geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true
957:       b.mat.opacity = clamp(b.life / b.max, 0, 1)
958:       if (b.life <= 0) {
959:         this.scene.remove(b.points)
960:         b.geo.dispose(); b.mat.dispose()
961:         this.bursts.splice(i, 1)
962:       }
963:     }
964:     for (let i = this.rings.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
965:       const r = this.rings[i]
966:       r.life -= dt
967:       const k = 1 - clamp(r.life / r.max, 0, 1)
968:       r.mesh.scale.setScalar(lerp(r.start, r.end, k))
969:       r.mat.opacity = (1 - k) * 0.8

But captureReady normal is `state='stagger'` and `alive` true (since weakened false) until capture. Actually checkThreshold sets captureReady but state stagger, alive true unless dead/captured/weakened. Good. Boss onBossDown sets weakened true, so alive false.

That may be okay for ranged bosses, but they won't chase. Could add approach. Fine.

content.text:
Let's make fixes then run browser. We need add tests too. First patch known bugs:

1. init title logic remove hide/re-show.
2. engageBoss make visible.
3. onBossLeash already.
4. hud FPS dt.
5. main world.burst optional -> use actual effect maybe fine. Could remove or implement world.burst? not needed since game.burst same pos. Replace `this.world.burst?.(...)` with none.
6. onOverlayClose duplicate.
7. paused Escape handling.
8. captureCreature: normal capture removes creature after 0.65; bond added. Boss bond never added even if party has room. Should give boss as bond maybe. For boss capture, currently no addBond. User may expect bosses? The codex bonded counts them. Could add boss bond if space. But final maybe not. Not essential.
9. `updateBossTriggers` final requires questStage>=3 and model.visible; unlockFinal calls `final.model.visible = true`; okay.
10. Player create root before start title; player visible on title? Game scene includes player at 9,84 — title camera looks toward x=2,z=62 so player maybe not in frame. Could hide player on title and show on start. Let's hide until start to avoid a random player in title view. But startGame sets visible? It doesn't. Add this.player.root.visible = false initially in init or constructor, and in startGame true. Yet player.respawn later. Good.
11. Title creatures spawn at positions with terrainHeight maybe on ground; good.
12. `this.hud.hideTitle?.()` method exists, but as noted hide timer. Just don't hide.
13. Sound toggle maybe starts audio only on click.
14. Game.loop starts after init; loading scene rendering blank first 1 sec; okay.
15. updatePlaying checks pausePressed at start and consumes. If Escape while pointer lock triggers browser exits lock + key event; onPointerLock pauses plus key consumed? mode changes. fine.
16. When codex open via Tab, overlay shown. Since mode paused, no key handling. Add else if mode paused updatePaused. Use input.consume('pausePressed') || codexPressed to close. But if opened from title-help, mode title-help and no key. Add.
17. `openOverlayStack` closes previous and pushes. But opening codex from pause then close should return to pause. Current close resumes. Could improve: close to previous. `closeOverlayStack` has logic to open top, but when codex was opened from pause, `openOverlayStack` closes pause without removing from stack? It actually: prev='pause', hud.closeOverlay('pause',true), then push 'codex' => stack ['pause','codex']. On close codex, idx removes codex, top 'pause' -> openOverlay('pause') then openPause. Good. But overlay stack from direct gameplay: openOverlayStack('codex') prev undefined, stack ['codex']; close -> empty resume. Good. Nice. PauseGame sets stack ['pause'].
18. But Escape pause while in codex: updatePaused calls closeOverlayStack(top) with 'codex' -> returns to pause. Another escape closes pause. Good.
19. resumeGame top close. If pause stack ['pause'] close then play. Good.
20. when openCodex direct from gameplay, mode paused but there is no pause panel, overlay stack ['codex']; close resumes. Fine.
21. `this.game.onSelectBond` not defined on Game. Clicking party slot does nothing. Add onSelectBond(index) in Game selecting active bond.
22. `this.hud.syncCompanion()` when none hides card. good.
23. `syncVitals` calls `updateHud` which also updates HUD and companion. Fine.
24. in captureCreature `this.hud.showCapture({ ...def, name: c.boss ? ...})` spread includes colors object, fine.
25. capture normal creature and `removed` then `world respawn`? captured not queued, so population decreases; but respawn only on defeated. For wild capture, should schedule respawn too. Otherwise capture all creatures eventually empty; okay but better queue. Add respawn queue for wild capture (not bosses) at 45s perhaps in else branch. Or population permanent capture expected. At least 3 per species and 8 species. Fine but world can feel empty. Add respawn later maybe.

26. type wheel labels. Fine.

27. `this.hud.hideLoading` called again startGame; timeout duplicate harmless.

28. In `startGame`, this.world.showWaypoint('nya'), fine.
29. `this.player.setStart` and player.root visible.
30. `this.player.respawnPoint.set(26, terrainHeight(...), 40)` Vector3 set correct.
31. `onPointerLock` pause on lock exit; clicking canvas requests lock, but when user presses Esc to pause, pointerlockchange fires with mode playing and hadLock -> pauseGame. Also key event pause -> pauseGame. Fine.

32. Main `respawn` does not reset bosses? resetBosses already death. Player respawn. Good. Does it reset quest? no.

33. `playerDie` called every frame? mode set dead, so updatePlaying not called. fine.

34. `capture()` on boss with `captureReady` but `alive` false (weakened) still update branch executes since update handles captured first. good.

35. `this.activeBoss` remains boss while weakened; updatePlaying calls hud.updateBoss and showBoss if weakened, so boss bar remains. after capture activeBoss null. fine.

36. Boss leash: `updateCombat` if d > leash*1.7 returns and calls onBossLeash, which sets dormant/hidden, activeBoss null. But c.update continues to after updateCombat and terrain follow, then updateBar; state dormant; it will animate. Fine. Need engage boss make visible again.

37. Final boss spawn at x=-2,z=-53 but SHRINES.tree is x=-2,z=-64. Boss visible false. unlockFinal shows it at -53 which is in front of tree. okay.

38. `finalCheck` only final boss; no ordinary victory. okay.

39. World shrines has no tree, but purifyShrine only for bosses. Final boss is tree; purifyShrine('tree') returns early. That's fine but no visual. Could add tree shrine? Not needed. But if `captureCreature` final adds 'tree' to purified; fine.

40. `hud.markBonded` for bosses; codex images present.

Let's patch.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')

content.text:
Potential issue: shared geometries/materials across model meshes? Creature models use shared `GEO` geometries and `mat` per call materials. Disposing a creature model will dispose shared GEO sphere/cone geometries globally! In Creature.remove, it traverses and disposes o.geometry (shared from models GEO), so all future creatures that use those geometries will break after one creature is removed! This is critical. Models use shared GEO objects. Creature.remove disposes all geometries and materials. Since GEO is module-level shared across all models, disposing a sphere from one creature will invalidate all other creatures/bosses, potentially after first wild death/capture. We haven't seen break yet because maybe removals occurred? Debug capture anansi did remove after 0.65; later scenes maybe broken but we reloaded. This is a major bug.

Similarly Player.companion.dispose traverses and disposes shared geometries from buildCreature. That means switching bonds disposes shared geometries used by wild creatures => broken. Also main title creatures disposal likewise disposes shared GEO geometries used by all. Very bad.

Need fix disposal strategy. Simplest: do not dispose geometries/materials for model objects, or clone geometries when building. Because all models use shared GEO, shared materials? Each `mat()` call creates a new material, but geometry shared. Sprites generated textures per sprite? glowSprite creates radialTexture each time new. Disposing is okay but not necessary.

Best: avoid disposing shared geometry in Creature.remove and Player.spawnCompanion and titleCreatures. Remove geometry disposal but maybe dispose materials (each unique) — materials are unique per model, but `flashMats` clones materials. Still safe. Yet some meshes may share materials within a model (e.g., same `dark` material for multiple parts), disposing multiple times okay. But cross-model sharing? model mats created per builder call, so unique. However static materials e.g. GEO? no.

But `buildCreature` uses `statusBar` with new materials each. Fine. So remove geometry disposal in Creature.remove and title creature cleanup and companion disposal. Player muzzle? no.

Main `disposeObject` used only enemyOrbs/soulOrbs/dropped orbs which use unique geometries, safe, but for soul orb buildSoulOrb creates unique geometry. Good.

But if disposeObject gets applied to creature? no.

Also main titleCreatures disposal uses `.geometry?.dispose` on shared. Fix.
Player companion removal geometry dispose fix.
Creature.remove geometry dispose fix.
Main `o.model.traverse` for playerOrbs/droppedOrbs use unique geo, safe.
Could add comment.

Additionally, spawnCompanion model's flash clones? no.

This is important. Also `canvasPortrait` scene.traverse disposes geometry from models built via buildCreature => same shared GEO! In canvasPortrait at line 231 disposes all o.geometry for the portrait model, which includes shared GEO. Game calls buildPortraits for 8 creatures, so after portraits are built, all shared geometry could be disposed! But models still render because disposed geometry buffers might still exist until render? Actually WebGLRenderer upload could fail or recreate? The portrait builder disposes geometry before any world rendering? Init order: world created first, then player, spawnWorld builds creatures (using geometry), then buildPortraits builds models and disposes geometries shared, breaking all world creatures. But our screenshots showed creatures rendered fine. Why? Because THREE BufferGeometry.dispose() emits event and renderer deallocates GPU buffers; if not yet uploaded, nothing; but geometry data still exists and next render re-uploads, so it works. Dispose is not fatal for BufferGeometry. It just frees GPU resources, re-upload next render. So not fatal, but repeated GPU churn. Still best avoid. In canvasPortrait, dispose only materials. Also `renderer2.dispose`. Fix to avoid disposing shared geo. This is critical-ish for performance but not rendering correctness. Do anyway.

Also buildPortraits each call uses buildCreature with new material clones. Good.

In `canvasPortrait`, `scene.traverse(o => { if (o.geometry) o.geometry.dispose() })` — remove.

Also main titleCreatures could be built from shared GEO; fix done.

Player `this.scene.remove` companion model and materials dispose; shared GEO safe.

Main model dispose for soul orbs unique; fine.

Creature remove disposes materials. If materials shared between body parts of same creature, disposing duplicate safe. If flashMats cloned from originals, originals not disposed? It replaces mesh material with clone, original material still referenced nowhere, not disposed. Memory leak. Could dispose originals when cloning? In constructor:
const origMat = o.material
o.material = origMat.clone()

Better collect unique base materials, clone and assign all meshes using them. Current code clones per mesh but does not dispose old. Each original material may be used by multiple meshes, leak only once per builder. Fine. No action.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable 3D Pokémon-style RPG set in Jamaica, with creatures based on mythology from different cultures and shooter mechanics included.

## Requirements
- 3D (Three.js) browser game.
- Jamaica-inspired setting.
- Monster roster drawn from different world mythologies.
- Include shooter mechanics.
- Responsive mobile/touch support expected by repository conventions.

## Decisions
- Title: **SOUL YARD — Legends of Pimento Isle**.
- Third-person over-the-shoulder action shooter, not turn-based combat.
- Shooter loop: weaken wild spirits with aether bolts, then throw soul orbs to capture/bond them.
- Jamaica-inspired fictional island zones: Pimento Beach, Nine Mile Village, Blue Mountain Rise, Luminous Reef, Silk Cotton Grove.
- Eight mythic creatures: Anansi, Rolling Calf, Mami Wata, Quetzalcoatl, Nian, Bakunawa, Kitsune, Raven.
- Three Warden bosses plus final boss Anansi Unbound; quest progression through shrine purification.
- Party of 4 active bonds, companion AI attacks, elemental type wheel, procedural models/audio/textures, no external 3D/audio assets.
- Desktop + mobile controls, HUD, minimap, compendium, dialogue, pause, death, victory screens.
- Vite + Three.js, generated portrait screenshots via offscreen renderer.

## Work State
### Completed
- All game modules written: `src/utils.js`, `src/terrain.js`, `src/constants.js`, `src/models.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/creatures.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/hud.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html`, `src/style.css`.
- Fixed build-blocking syntax error in `src/constants.js`.
- `npm install` and `npm run build` now succeed.
- Fixed runtime crash in `World.buildDistantLand()` by checking `o.isMesh` before assigning `material.fog`.
- Removed duplicated `consumeSlot()` call and stale `distanceTo` import in `player.js`.
- Fixed bond stat recalculation so crit/other bonuses reset on switch.
- Fixed title transition so title no longer auto-hides after loader.
- Fixed boss re-engage visibility, overlay close duplicate condition, paused-mode keyboard handling, title-help escape handling.
- Added HUD FPS timing based on actual `dt`.
- Added party-slot bond selection via `Game.onSelectBond` and codex entry selection via `onSelectBondById`.
- Added mobile pause button and binding.
- Added mobile HUD layout fixes: hid party bar, moved orb counter under vitals, moved minimap above joystick, moved boss bar higher.
- Added touch title instruction line.
- Fixed quick-tap fire handling by consuming `firePressed` and calling `input.endFrame()` each frame.
- Fixed soul-orb spawn using mutated direction vector.
- Added disposal fixes after discovering shared model geometry: removed geometry disposal from creatures/companions/title models/portraits.
- Added cleanup/disposal for enemy orbs and beam effects.
- Fixed beam telegraph lifecycle and decorative beam cleanup.
- Cleared boss dashes when boss leashes.
- Added `tests/game.test.mjs` with 8 tests; `npm test` passes all tests.
- Verified in browser:
  - Desktop title screen renders and fits after responsive CSS fix.
  - Auto-start `?play=1&quality=low` enters gameplay.
  - Elder Nya dialogue completes and grants Kitsune bond; quest advances to stage 1.
  - Boss intro, warden weakening/capture, quest progress `1 / 3 wardens`, final boss unlock (`tree` waypoint), final capture and victory screen all work.
  - Death screen and respawn work.
  - Mobile title, gameplay, pause, codex render.
  - Mobile fire works while held; mobile pause opens pause overlay.
  - Controlled orb throw test captured an Anansi and added it to party.

### Active
- Final browser verification pass after recent internal fixes:
  - Re-check world rendering after geometry-disposal changes.
  - Re-test capture via actual thrown orb with corrected spawn offset.
  - Verify boss beam effects no longer leak.
  - Check final boss flow again after beam/cleanup changes.
  - Inspect desktop/mobile screenshots for remaining visual issues.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Reload desktop and mobile pages; confirm no console errors after latest changes.
2. Re-test real capture flow with a wild spirit using orb throw and confirm bond/party/HUD update.
3. Re-test boss engagement, weakening, capture, final boss, victory after cleanup changes.
4. Verify mobile boss bar and touch HUD layout after CSS changes.
5. Review remaining visual issues: title card portraits, giant/flat glow effects seen near canopy, boss model clipping at close range.
6. Add README or documentation only if needed; then review git diff and commit if requested.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game orchestration, modes, projectiles, quests, bosses, cleanup, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creatures.js`: wild creature and boss AI/combat/capture.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: movement, camera, shooting, companion, HUD sync.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: procedural island and props.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`: player/creature procedural models.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/hud.js`: DOM UI, minimap, compass, codex, dialogue.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/constants.js`: creatures, bosses, types, NPCs, balance data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: title/HUD/mobile/overlay styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game DOM shell and overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/game.test.mjs`: passing terrain/type/capture helper tests.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: browser verification screenshots.

## Important Context
- Working directory is a PlayGround repo; all game files are newly created and uncommitted.
- Runtime serves on port `3002` via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`; tmux session `soul` is running it.
- Use `playwright-cli` sessions `soul` (desktop) and `mobile` (iPhone 15 emulation); Chromium was installed with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.
- Environment is CPU software rendering: `ANGLE (Mesa, Vulkan ... llvmpipe)`; game auto-selects `quality=low`.
- `?play=1` auto-starts gameplay; `?quality=low` forces low quality.
- `window.__soulYard` debug API supports `start`, `teleport(x,z)`, `look(yaw,pitch)`, `boss(shrine)`, `purify(n)`, `captureNearest`, `attackNearest`, `state`, `hud`, `player`, `world`.
- `window.__soulYard.look` is on the debug API, not on `game`.
- Headed browser under Xvfb is heavily throttled, so `game.time` advances slowly even though code is correct.
- Shared procedural geometries in `models.js` must not be disposed per instance.
- Latest build/test state: `npm run build` passes; `npm test` passes 8/8.
